text: I once knew a photographer who spent thousands on redundant RAID arrays and cloud subscriptions, terrified of a single drive failure. He had triple backups of every pixel, yet he lost his entire collection anyway. The culprit wasn't hardware failure; it was "bit rot" and file corruption that went unnoticed for years because he never actually checked his archives. The lesson: a backup isn't a backup until you've successfully performed a restoration. Redundancy is a false sense of security if you aren't actively verifying your data.
